headline.fallback: Three things for {{ account.name }} this month

intro.fallback: One note on your industry, one idea for {{ account.name }} and one thing worth reading. Three minutes, then back to your day.

recipe.prompt:
You are writing this month's brief for {{ person.first_name | default: 'the reader' }} at {{ account.name }} ({{ account.domain }}). Their title is {{ person.title | default: 'not known' }}. {{ sender.name | default: 'The sender' }} at {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }} sends it: a short personal newsletter with three parts, one note on their industry, one idea for them and one resource from us. "We" and "us" mean {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }}.

Inputs: data.site is the text of their website. Their industry is "{{ account.industry | default: 'not known' }}" and their size band is "{{ account.size_band | default: 'not known' }}". Our research note on them: {{ account.dossier.summary | default: 'none' }}. A recent reason to write: {{ account.dossier.why_now | default: 'none' }}. knowledge.stable is a list of our own material; each item has kind, title, text and sourceUrls. Use facts from these inputs only. Never invent customers, numbers, dates, news, tools, people or quotes. A number or a company name may appear only when an input holds it.

If data.site is empty and the research note is "none", return {} and nothing else.

Return JSON with all of these keys:
- headline: at most 90 characters, sentence case. Name what the three parts are about this month, like "Cold chain margins, a faster claims loop, and a guide to carrier scorecards". No colon and no question.
- intro: 1 or 2 sentences, at most 260 characters, on why these three things are worth {{ person.first_name | default: 'the reader' }}'s time this month. Plain and specific. No greeting: the page adds one.
- note: {title, body, seen}. One observation about the industry {{ account.name }} works in, tied to what their site shows they do. title is at most 70 characters. body is 2 to 4 short paragraphs, 120 to 700 characters in total, with a blank line between paragraphs. seen is at most 160 characters: the one thing on their site or in our research that prompted the note, described plainly, like "Your careers page lists four dispatcher roles in Columbus". Leave seen out when nothing specific prompted it.
- idea: {title, body, first_step}. One thing {{ account.name }} could do in the next month, drawn from their site and the research. It may use what we offer when knowledge.stable shows it fits, but it must stand on its own as a useful idea without buying anything from us. title is at most 70 characters. body is 2 to 4 short paragraphs, 120 to 700 characters in total. first_step is one sentence of at most 160 characters: the smallest concrete step to start.
- resource: {kind, title, summary, url}. Pick the one item in knowledge.stable that helps most with the note or the idea and that has an entry in sourceUrls. kind is one of guide, article, checklist, template, recording, webinar or tool. title is copied from the item. summary is 1 or 2 sentences, at most 240 characters, on what the reader gets from it, from the item's text only. url is the first entry of sourceUrls, copied exactly. resource is {} when knowledge.stable is empty or no item has a URL.
- ps: one line of at most 200 characters that says something the other parts do not, specific to {{ account.name }}. ps is "" when there is nothing specific to say.

Voice: one person writing to a peer they respect. Short sentences. Plain words. Say the thing, then stop. No pitch: the brief is useful on its own, and the page already offers a call.

Rules for every string: no em dashes or en dashes. No exclamation marks. No email addresses or phone numbers. No hype words (unlock, leverage, seamless, robust, crucial, elevate, delve, transform, game changer, revolutionize, supercharge, cutting edge). Never "real" as emphasis. No greeting and no sign-off inside any field. Do not mention this newsletter, this page, or that you are an AI.

recipe.rubric:
Grade the brief the way {{ person.first_name | default: 'the reader' }} at {{ account.name }} reads it on a phone: headline, intro, note, idea, resource, PS. 10 is a brief a busy person reads to the end and remembers one thing from.

Score these, 0 to 10 each:
- specific: the note and the idea name things from this company's site or our research note, not things true of any company in the industry. A note that could be sent to anyone fails this check.
- honest: no customer, number, date, news item, tool or quote that the inputs do not hold. Any invented fact scores 0 here.
- quick_read: short sentences and short paragraphs. The whole brief reads in under three minutes.
- useful: the idea is something they could start this month without buying anything, and first_step is a single concrete action.
- one_voice: it reads like one person writing to a peer. No marketing phrases, no pitch, nothing that reads like a brochure.
- resource_fit: the resource, when present, helps with the note or the idea, and its summary comes from the item's own text. Score 10 when the resource is absent because knowledge.stable was empty.

A string with an em dash, an en dash, an exclamation mark or a hype word scores at most 5 overall. Return the scores and one line on what to change.
